account: Today I made my market walk, attended tea with the neighbour on the east bank, and returned to the office, though late for the 16:30 appointment. The neighbour mentioned a vague bridge or port change rumour but had no firsthand evidence. The secretary likewise reported no confirmed proposal or new correspondence, so I have no basis to treat that rumour as fact. The secretary confirmed tomorrow's mill grain inspection and came to my home tonight to explain its checklist: quantities, storage conditions, and supply concerns, with observations and follow-up decisions recorded. Builder has now come to my door at 20:36 asking for a personal inspection of completed great hall lighting tomorrow at 18:00. These evening visits have interrupted my sleep and are somewhat unusual, but their stated purposes are ordinary town business. I have not seen the lighting work myself and have not yet agreed to the requested appointment. I should review the appointment book and checklist in the morning.
